newsitem.title: SUDAN: Pro-government forces repel Sudan rebels - paper.
newsitem.headline: Pro-government forces repel Sudan rebels - paper.

text.p: A Sudanese newspaper said on Wednesday that forces loyal to the Khartoum government had repelled an attack on its positions by southern rebels.

The private newspaper Alwan said the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) of John Garang last week attacked the SPLA/Bahr al-Ghazal group's positions in Wun Rog, 150 km (95 miles) north of Wau, the south's second largest town.
"The outcome of the attack was huge losses in men and weaponry to the rebel Garang's forces," the daily said.
According to Alwan, the Bahr al-Ghazal group, headed by Kerubino Kwanyin Bol seized 315 Kalashnikov guns, 17 mortars and two heavy machineguns and took 100 SPLA soldiers prisoners.
Bol's forces also seized Akak airport, which is equipped with modern telecommunications, the paper said.
It quoted Faustino Wobanag, spokesman of the SPLA/Bahr al-Ghazal group, as saying the aim of the rebel attack was to take Gogrial, some 100 km (60 miles) north of Wau.
The Bahr al-Ghazal group, which has split from the mainstream SPLA, signed a peace charter with the government of Lieutenant-General Omar Hassan al-Bashir a year ago.
Garang refuses to sign the charter, saying the Khartoum government is not serious about peace.

His group and the opposition National Democratic Alliance (NDA) have launched attacks on government positions on three fronts this year. The government says Eritrean, Ethiopian and Ugandan troops are doing most of the fighting but the three states deny this.
